desc: Cape Comorin, also known as Kanyakumari, is the southernmost tip of the Indian mainland, located at the confluence of the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean. It is a major pilgrimage and tourist destination famous for its spectacular sunrise and sunset views. The Vivekananda Rock Memorial, built on a small island just off the cape, commemorates Swami Vivekananda's meditation visit in 1892. The Thiruvalluvar Statue, a 133-foot tall stone sculpture adjacent to the memorial, honors the Tamil poet. The cape is known for its distinctive multi-colored sands.
fact: It is the southernmost tip of the Indian mainland at the tri-ocean confluence · The Vivekananda Rock Memorial honors Swami Vivekananda's 1892 visit · The 133-foot Thiruvalluvar Statue stands adjacent to the memorial · It is famous for spectacular sunrise and sunset views over three seas

desc: Kanyakumari Cape, historically known as Cape Comorin, marks the southernmost point of the Indian subcontinent. The cape is named after the deity Kanyakumari, an incarnation of the goddess Parvati, and houses the ancient Kumari Amman Temple. The bay area features unique phenomena where the waters of the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea can be distinguished by their colors. The cape attracts millions of pilgrims and tourists annually, especially during the full moon when the sun and moon are visible simultaneously on opposite horizons. The area is protected as a biosphere reserve for its coastal biodiversity.
fact: It is the southernmost point of the Indian subcontinent named after goddess Kanyakumari · The waters of the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea have distinct visible colors at the cape · Full moon offers simultaneous sun and moon opposite horizon views · The area is protected as a biosphere reserve

desc: Point Calimere, also known as Kodikkarai, is a low-lying headland on the Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu. It is the southernmost point of the Coromandel Coast and the easternmost point of Tamil Nadu. The area is protected as the Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary, a Ramsar site. The cape is the only known breeding ground of the great flamingo in southern India. It features a unique ecosystem of tidal swamps, mudflats, and tropical dry evergreen forests. The cape was historically a significant landmark for maritime navigation along the Coromandel Coast.
fact: It is the easternmost point of Tamil Nadu on the Coromandel Coast · The Point Calimere Sanctuary is a Ramsar site for migratory birds · It is the only known great flamingo breeding ground in southern India · It features unique tidal swamps and tropical dry evergreen forests

desc: Dhanushkodi is a cape at the southeastern tip of Pamban Island in Tamil Nadu, forming the Indian terminus of the Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu) chain of limestone shoals connecting India to Sri Lanka. The cape was home to a thriving town before it was devastated by the 1964 Rameswaram cyclone, which destroyed the town and killed over 1,800 people. The ruins of the ghost town remain as a tourist attraction. The cape marks the closest point between India and Sri Lanka at just 29 km. The surrounding Gulf of Mannar is a UNESCO Marine Biosphere Reserve with rich coral reefs and dugong populations.
fact: Dhanushkodi forms the Indian side of the Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu) shoals to Sri Lanka · The town was destroyed by the 1964 Rameswaram cyclone, now a ghost town · It is the closest point between India and Sri Lanka at 29 km · The surrounding Gulf of Mannar is a UNESCO Marine Biosphere Reserve
